comment: Budgets of the latency gate (performance spec, benches/latency_gate.rs) on the reference runner (ho-z10). Targets are configuration: change them here, with a recorded reason, never in code. Every gated value is the median over the gate's rounds of a per-round p99 (or of the throughput). 4MB proxy overhead set to 16 ms: a loaded shared host showed p99 tails near 12 ms at a 4.6 ms median.

speed.comment: The machine speed the budgets were set at, per reference CPU. Before every round the gate times a fixed workload (SHA-256 over 256 KiB, best of five). A measurement's budget is multiplied by its CPU's budget_factor, and again by how much longer than that CPU's reference_calibration_us its rounds took at the median (never less than 1, at most max_slowdown); a throughput floor is divided instead. A CPU not listed has its budgets compared as written. The calibration time only compares a CPU with itself (a CPU without SHA extensions takes several times longer at the same overall speed), so each CPU has its own reference. Intel Core Ultra 7 155U: the budgets were written for it; ho-z10 runs that met every budget measured 130 to 145 us. Main CI on 2026-11-24 failed request, protect and throughput budgets together while measuring about 2.4 times slower everywhere, including the direct baseline: the 15 W CPU throttles under heat and load. Intel Core i7-10510U: a second node of the ho-z10 runner set since 2026-11-24. A run that met every budget measured 1110 to 1330 us; against the 155U's median it was 1.0 to 1.75 times slower per measurement (1.5 for redaction throughput), hence budget_factor 1.5. A run at 1400 to 1650 us measured about 2 times the 155U median and passes with the stretch. The regression check compares relative to the same calibration, and only runs on the same CPU.

engine.comment: Added request latency through the LLM proxy with the production engine (outgoing::prepare, scrim-redact redactor and guard). request_p99_ms: the redaction benchmark's 1 MB bodies seen for the first time (the guard's verdict cache is cleared before every sample). Before the guard's decoder prefilters (PR #153 on ho-z10): p50 24 to 29 ms, p99 31 to 42 ms across 10, 1,000 and 10,000 secrets, budget 60 ms. With them (PR #183 on ho-z10, Core Ultra 7 155U, three runs): p50 7.6 to 21 ms, p99 9.8 to 27 ms; budget 40 ms, about 1.5 times the highest p99. next_turn_p99_ms: an agent's next turn, the previous 1 MB request again with the cache_control marker moved and one new exchange, right after the previous one (performance spec, 'Added request latency budget'). PR #183 on ho-z10: before the cut search used memrchr3, p50 5.4 to 8.8 ms, p99 8.2 to 11.7 ms (slowdown 1.3); after, p50 3.9, 4.6 and 5.5 ms and p99 4.7, 6.8 and 7.8 ms for 10, 1,000 and 10,000 secrets, so the spec's initial 5 ms target for 1,000 secrets is not met reliably: about 1 ms of it is the guard (cuts, BLAKE3 over the body, the new segments), the rest the codec's JSON plan and the redactor over the whole body, which are not cached. On a Xeon W-2295 the same measurement is 3.7 to 5 ms at p50. Budgets 10 ms (10 and 1,000 secrets) and 12 ms (10,000) held it there. Set to the spec's 5 ms (10 and 1,000 secrets) and 7 ms (10,000, spec 10 ms) by the next-turn caches PR (redactor segment cache, codec plan cache, guard runs): on the Xeon W-2295, pinned to one core, A/B against PR #183 in two rounds each, p50 3.3, 3.8, 4.2 ms to 2.0, 2.2, 2.6 ms and p99 3.7 to 4.8 ms to 2.1 to 3.2 ms for 10, 1,000 and 10,000 secrets; the same run cut proxy overhead's plan out of the next turn but adds about 0.35 ms per MB to proxy_overhead (plan cache filled on first sight, 1MB p50 1.1 to 1.5 ms, budget 3 ms unchanged) and about 1 ms per MB to first-sight request and protect (budgets unchanged).

core.comment: The redaction core on its own, as the scrim-redact benchmarks measure it: Snapshot::protect per 1 MB request with the default thread count, and single-thread Redactor::redact throughput (the per-core minimum of the performance spec). Measured on ho-z10 (PR #153): protect p99 21 to 47 ms; redact throughput 0.76 to 2.4 GB/s on one core. The runner's CPU (a 15 W laptop part) changes clock with load and heat, and one run measured half the throughput of the previous one for the same code. Budgets therefore sit well outside that range (protect 60 ms, throughput floors at about half the slowest run); the regression check, which compares relative to a calibration workload, catches smaller changes. protect_p99_ms set to 30 ms (from 60) in PR #183: with the guard's decoder prefilters ho-z10 measured protect p99 7.7 to 18.3 ms on a first-sight 1 MB body (cache cleared before every sample); 30 ms is about 1.5 times the highest.

regression.comment: The regression check against the previous release (scripts/perfgate). Each gated statistic is compared as the median of its rounds. It regresses when worse than the baseline by more than threshold + noise_factor x the larger relative spread (median absolute deviation) of the two runs' rounds, capped at max_allowed, and by more than the unit's floor. With calibrate, each round's value is taken relative to the time of a fixed workload (SHA-256 over 256 KiB) measured just before it, so a run on a slower clock is not a regression. Only runs on the same reference conditions (the match fields) are compared. enforce false (report only, set 2026-11-25): on the shared ho-z10 runner set, 14 runs of the same code on the same CPU spread 2.5 to 4 times per measurement (passthrough 1 MB p50 0.75 to 2.0 ms, protect p99 and redaction throughput alike), with or without calibration; a single baseline run then fails PRs and releases at random beyond any threshold that still catches a regression. The absolute budgets above remain the hard gate. Set enforce to true once the gate runs on a dedicated runner whose runs agree within the threshold.
